summary: Built `jailfs`, a standard-library-only Python 3 package giving agent programs one writable directory plus disjoint read-only roots, with every path walked one component at a time through a per-root directory fd using `dir_fd=` and `O_NOFOLLOW`, so the kernel refuses `..`, links and escapes. Writes go only to the writable root through an exclusively created, randomly named temporary file renamed into place, plus a shadow check, an opened-file identity set and a per-`batch()` duplicate check. Every refusal is a `Refused` with a code and a fix, and 145 unittest tests (all passing) plus a 14-mutation check script prove each fix is really pinned by a test.

pattern_mapping.Start-up check: jailfs/workspace.py: `Workspace.__init__` + `_make_root` + `_check_disjoint` (one writable root, roots resolved once via `Root.real`, overlapping roots refused)
pattern_mapping.Writable and read roots: `Root` (given spelling, resolved spelling, one `fd`); `Workspace._writable` and `Workspace._read_roots`, in lookup order via `_roots`
pattern_mapping.Locator: `_normalise` (lexical, refuses a climb above the root), `_absolute_parts` (lexical longest-prefix match against `(root.given, root.real)`), `_locate_read` / `_locate_write` returning `Location(root, rel)`
pattern_mapping.Root handle: `Root.fd` plus `_walk_dirs` (opens each directory component with `os.open(..., dir_fd=prev, O_NOFOLLOW|O_DIRECTORY)`), `_open_file`, `_lstat_in_root`
pattern_mapping.Writer: `_write_atomic`: `O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW` random temp name in the target's own directory, write+fsync, `os.rename(src_dir_fd=..., dst_dir_fd=...)`, identity taken after the rename; `_inspect_target` refuses links, directories and non-regular targets
pattern_mapping.Shadow check: `_shadow_in` (lstat of the resulting relative name in each read root, whatever the spelling), called from `save`
pattern_mapping.Opened set: `Workspace._opened` / `_written` as `(st_dev, st_ino)` identities; `read`/`load` add on open, `_write_atomic` adds after the rename; checked in `save` step 5
pattern_mapping.Loader: `Workspace.load` — extension check for `.py`/`.js`, then `read()` through the locator; there is no other loading attribute on the workspace
pattern_mapping.Refusal vocabulary: jailfs/errors.py: `Refused(code, message, fix)` with `E_ACCESS`, `E_NOT_FOUND`, `E_DUPLICATE`, `E_SHADOW`; `_refuse_oserror` maps every `OSError` so none escapes
pattern_mapping.Per-run duplicate check: `Workspace.batch()` context manager + `_batch_saved` set, keyed on the normalised relative name

notes_applied: Note 1 (let the operating system enforce the root): no string fallback; the path is opened component by component from the root's directory fd with `O_NOFOLLOW|O_DIRECTORY` and the last component with `O_NOFOLLOW`, `lstat`/`fstat` for type. Every link is refused, inside the root or not.

Note 2 (resolve roots once, never the agent's path): `Root.real = realpath(given)` at start-up; absolute agent paths are matched lexically with `os.path.normpath` against both `given` and `real`; `realpath` is never called on an agent path (mutation `m09` proves a test goes red if it is).
Note 3 (keep the roots disjoint): read root inside the writable root, writable root inside a read root, identical roots and nested/duplicate read roots all refuse at construction with a fix.

Note 4 (exclusive random temp name, then rename): `.jailfs-tmp-<hex>` created with `O_CREAT|O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW`; a planted file or link is skipped (EEXIST/ELOOP retry) and never followed; `rename` means a hard link to an input cannot carry a write (tested).

Note 5 (identities, not names; written exemption): `(st_dev, st_ino)` in `_opened`; the written identity is taken *after* the rename so a session may re-save its own output; hard-linked files are not refused.
Note 6 (a save can shadow a read-only file): `E_SHADOW` is raised when the resulting relative name exists in any read root, checked for relative, absolute and `sub/../` spellings.

Note 7 (one way to load code): `load` is the only loader, goes through the locator, and refuses non-`.py`/`.js` names and files outside the roots; a test asserts no `require`/`open`-like attribute exists.
Note 8 (strict flags): a list or tuple `root` is refused at construction with a fix naming `reads=[DIR]` (the Python form of `--root` once); `reads` as a bare string is refused too.
Note 9 (same names everywhere): `Location.label` shows writable-root files relatively and read-root files absolutely, and refusals use it.

Note 10 (order of refusals): shape/access → duplicate → shadow → replacing an opened file; `save` performs them in exactly that order and a test pins that a link is refused as `E_ACCESS` before the shadow check.

Note 11 (test that a regression test fails without its fix): `tools/mutation_check.py` — 14 mutations, each with the named tests that must go red, run one at a time, and a baseline that requires them green; it found five vacuous tests, which I rewrote.
tests: 145 unittest tests in five modules (tests/test_startup.py 21, tests/test_read.py 42, tests/test_save.py 40, tests/test_holes.py 23, tests/test_edges.py 19), run with `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests`; last result: `Ran 145 tests in 0.117s — OK`. Additionally `python3 tools/mutation_check.py` reports `48 checks, 0 failures` (24 named regression tests green in the baseline, each red under its own mutation).
chapter_feedback: The Structure table and the Sketch mapped almost one-to-one onto the required interface, which made the design fast; the 'refusal kinds stand for your own vocabulary' remark was essential for fitting the chapter's shape/access/shadow onto TASK.md's four codes.

The chapter understates one thing it later states correctly: the link refusal is *not* what stops a dangling-symlink escape in a writer built from exclusive create plus rename (note 4 plus note 5). My mutation run proved that deleting the link refusal alone leaves the escape test green; only restoring an in-place write makes it red. Worth a sentence in the Solution: the writer's shape is the hole-1 fix, the link refusal is the clear refusal on top.

Note 1 said to walk components and lstat the last component; I had to discover that `O_NOFOLLOW` applies only to the final component, so the walk is mandatory rather than advisory. The chapter says this implicitly ('walk the path one component at a time') but the reason could be spelled out.

The chapter does not say what a *relative* name should do when the writable root's copy is a link or a directory and a read root has a real file of that name: falling through would make the writable root a trampoline. I chose 'any non-ENOENT refusal stops the lookup' and had to guess.
Note 6 warns about warns-vs-refuses but the interface has no warning channel, so `E_SHADOW` is the only option; the chapter could say what a library with no logger should do.

Note 10 gives an order for refusals but the four codes overlap (a save onto a link inside a read root could be access, shadow or duplicate), so the order had to be turned into a concrete precedence in code; an example of the resulting precedence chain would help.

Note 11 was the most valuable note in practice: it caught five tests that were green for the wrong reason (a redundant S_ISREG check, a shadow check confound, and a `realpath` case where the resolved link landed in a read root, so the right code came from the wrong rule).

The chapter's claim that the opened set protects the agent's view rather than the input's bytes matched what the mutations showed, but a reader could easily build the set and believe it is a containment mechanism; the Consequences list could say this more loudly.
